title: QUIC Non-HTTP/3 Interop-Testcase Inventory Work Item
summary: Add a canonical inventory/profile slice that enumerates every documented non-HTTP/3 upstream QUIC testcase, classifies each case explicitly, and keeps per-cell artifact retention without claiming broad interop readiness.
planned_changes:
- Add a non-HTTP/3 inventory/profile slice to SPEC-QUIC-INT.
- Classify the documented upstream QUIC testcases into supported, intentionally unsupported, prerequisite-blocked, or not-mappable cells.
- Keep HTTP/3 out of scope.
- Preserve per-cell artifact retention and avoid generic unsupported fallthrough for the inventoried cases.
- Update the interop prep plan and gap ledger so the new goal is visible before code changes start.
out_of_scope: turning every inventory cell green immediately
verification_plan: Review the upstream QUIC testcase inventory from quic-interop-runner documentation, verify the new requirement and architecture classify each testcase explicitly, run any helper dry-run planning necessary to emit the inventory/profile, and finish with SpecTrace plus Workbench validation.
completion_notes: Helper inventory plumbing is in progress. REQ-QUIC-INT-0018 now has direct requirement-home proof in tests/Incursa.Quic.Tests/RequirementHomes/INT/REQ-QUIC-INT-0018.cs. The documented non-HTTP/3 inventory is now explicit in the helper and per-run artifacts, versionnegotiation, keyupdate, and resumption are now green, chacha20 remains blocked pending CipherSuitesPolicy support, and dry-run proof now preserves zerortt, v2, rebind-port, rebind-addr, and connectionmigration as prerequisite-blocked until each runtime or proof prerequisite is closed case by case. Zerortt remains blocked specifically on full hosted/Linux runner success, client-side 0-RTT request-stream/packet-analysis proof, and harness classification; client-side probe emission, server-role dispatch, hosted workflow wiring, resumption PSK acceptance, internal admission-gate proof, bounded internal early-data runtime proof, local X25519 proof, or runtime queued-final-stream proof is not enough. The server-role harness path enables managed resumption tickets plus server early-data admission for runner-driven zerortt attempts, the 2026-05-09 local Windows attempt under artifacts/interop-runner/server-zerortt-quic-go/20260509-114555424-server-nginx/ failed before Incursa execution on the upstream testcase long filename setup path, and the manual hosted workflow exposes an advisory `zerortt-server-proof` profile for the Linux attempt. Hosted run `25608915721` on 2026-05-09 reached managed server execution, explicit inventory/report output, quic-go 0-RTT emission, and one served request stream, but failed because the then-current P-256-only server crypto floor sent HelloRetryRequest for quic-go's hybrid/X25519 first-flight key-share offer and quic-go rejected 0-RTT after HRR. REQ-QUIC-CRT-0154 locally proves bounded server first-flight X25519 acceptance for that captured offer. Hosted run `25617591021` moved past the key-share/HRR symptom and exposed a queued-final STREAM+FIN flush failure under transient congestion; commit `e7dece89` fixed that runtime path with focused RFC 9000 stream-send proof. Hosted run `25617834482` on 2026-05-10 reached managed response/download success, with the client exiting 0 and downloaded-file checking succeeding, but runner packet analysis still failed with `0-RTT size: 10618`, `1-RTT size: 16499`, and `Client sent too much data in 1-RTT packets.` Resumption has source-level managed server NewSessionTicket issuance, PSK acceptance, managed SSLKEYLOGFILE export, and a live 2026-05-09 quic-interop-runner success artifact under artifacts/interop-runner/20260509-001723585-both-quic-go/.
